strings.name: Paul Milgrom
strings.summary: Milgrom applies auction and information economics to real markets, studying bidders’ knowledge, strategies and trading rules. With Wilson and others he designed spectrum auctions, then worked with computer scientists on broadcast-spectrum reallocation. He shared the 2020 economics Nobel and has extended market design to resources such as surface water.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Develops auction theory and spectrum-auction design, applying economics to public-resource allocation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Michigan mathematics AB (1970); Stanford doctorate formally awarded in 1979.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Theory into rules
strings.highlights.h1.text: Studies bidding information and incentives and helps design implementable auctions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Interdisciplinary market design
strings.highlights.h2.text: Works across economics and computing on spectrum and water-market constraints.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Surface-water chapter published
strings.timeline.t1.text: With Billy Ferguson, examined water rights, regulatory externalities and transaction costs.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won with Robert Wilson for auction theory and new auction formats.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Spectrum-reallocation study
strings.timeline.t3.text: With Leyton-Brown and Segal, examined the economics and computer science of spectrum reallocation.
strings.timeline.t4.title: US spectrum-auction design
strings.timeline.t4.text: Rules developed with Wilson and others entered FCC simultaneous multiple-round auctions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Returned to Stanford
strings.timeline.t5.text: Moved back to his alma mater to pursue theory and institutional design.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Auction theory with Weber
strings.timeline.t6.text: Their paper analyzed auction formats and bidders’ information.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate formally awarded
strings.timeline.t7.text: Finished the dissertation the previous year; degree awarded in 1979, followed by Northwestern teaching.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed mathematics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Worked in actuarial practice before turning to academic research.
